request.description: 35-year-old earning $95k in TX, contributing 10% to 401(k), wondering about catch-up eligibility and projected balance at 65

tax_implications.ira_phase_out_warning: Roth IRA — no deductibility phase-out applies. Roth contributions are always after-tax.

recommendations.message: You're contributing 10% to your 401(k) — above the minimum recommended 6% to capture your full employer match.
You're maxing out your Roth IRA ($7,000/year). Great choice given your income level — Roth grows tax-free.
At your current rate, you're projected to have ~$2.1M at retirement, generating ~$7,100/month using the 4% withdrawal rule.
Catch-up contributions ($7,500 extra 401k + $1,000 extra IRA) become available at age 50. You have 15 years to consider increasing contributions before then.
